title: The 10 Best Corded LED Work Lights
subtitle: Tripod and hanging LED work lights for job sites, garages and remodels, ranked from live Amazon data.
intro: A corded LED work light floods a room, garage or job site with daylight-white light all day without a battery. We ranked 10 best-sellers on rating, review volume and features (a wet-location or IP66 rating, a stated wattage, dimming or color control and a telescoping tripod). Be careful with brightness claims: most budget lights quote 21,000-32,000 lumens without a test standard. A listed wattage is a better reality check, since today's LEDs make roughly 100-150 lumens per watt. They run from about $49 for Wufoty's 2-head tripod light to $120 for LUTEC's tripod light or NS's 150 W hanging light.

avoid.name: YKXJM Work Lights with Stand, 14000 Lumen, 2 Adjustable Heads LED Work Light
avoid.flag: Sold as 14,000 lumens and 21,000 lumens at once
avoid.verdict: A tripod light whose listing gives two different brightness figures. The Wufoty is $5 more, with the same 2-head design and one consistent 14,000-lumen claim.
reasons: The title says 14,000 lumens; the first bullet says '21000LM super bright'. That's a 50% difference on the number the light is sold on.
The listing gives no wattage, so neither lumen figure can be sanity-checked.
It gives no voltage or weather rating, though it's sold for outdoor job sites.

buyers_guide.q: How many lumens do I need?
buyers_guide.a: 5,000-10,000 real lumens light a garage bay or room well. Budget lights often claim 20,000-30,000 lumens without a test standard; a stated wattage keeps them honest, since good LEDs produce roughly 100-150 lumens per watt.
Tripod lights aim where you're working and move with you. Hanging caged lights light a whole room evenly from above, which is better for drywall, painting and framing.

buyers_guide.q: Do I need a weather rating?
buyers_guide.a: For outdoor or wet sites, yes. Look for IP65/IP66 or an ETL or UL wet-location listing. Indoor-only lights can fail or shock in the rain.
5000-6500K daylight white shows colors and defects clearly, which is what you want for paint and finish work. Warmer 3000K is easier on the eyes for long sessions.

buyers_guide.q: Do LED work lights get hot?
buyers_guide.a: Far less than halogen, which is why they replaced them. Aluminum housings still get warm, so keep them away from plastic sheeting and flammable materials.
